source: NCERT Class XI, Statistics for Economics, Ch. 2 (Collection of Data).

sections.heading: 1. Sources of Data
points: **Data** = information collected for a statistical enquiry.
**Primary data** — collected **first-hand** by the investigator for a specific purpose (original).
**Secondary data** — already collected by someone else (from published sources — census, reports, newspapers).

sections.heading: 2. Methods of Collecting Primary Data
points: **Direct personal interview** — investigator personally contacts respondents.
**Indirect oral investigation** — questioning third parties who know the informant.
**Information from correspondents** — local agents send information.
**Mailed questionnaire** — questionnaire sent by post to respondents.
**Questionnaire filled by enumerators** — trained enumerators fill in responses (used in the Census).

sections.heading: 3. Questionnaire and Sampling
points: A good **questionnaire** should be short, clear, non-personal, logically ordered, with pre-coded options.

sub: **Census (complete enumeration)** — every unit of the population is studied (e.g. Population Census).
**Sample survey** — only a **representative part (sample)** is studied, and results generalised.

points: **Random sampling** avoids bias; a sample saves time, cost and effort.

sections.heading: 4. Sources / Agencies in India
points: **Census of India** (every 10 years) — the largest complete enumeration.
**National Sample Survey (NSSO/NSO)** — conducts large sample surveys (employment, consumption).
Errors: **sampling errors** (from studying a sample) and **non-sampling errors** (measurement, non-response, bias).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Primary data = first-hand (original); Secondary data = already collected by others.
Primary methods: direct interview, indirect oral, correspondents, mailed questionnaire, enumerators.
Census = complete enumeration; Sample survey = representative part.
Census of India = every 10 years; NSSO = large sample surveys.
Errors: sampling and non-sampling.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Primary data = collected first-hand**; **secondary data = already collected by others**.
**Census = studies every unit**; **sample survey = studies a representative part**.
The **Census of India** is conducted **every 10 years**.
**Sampling errors** arise only in sample surveys; **non-sampling errors** can occur in both.
